description: Moxi 2.0 is the next-generation hospital mobile-manipulation platform whose rollout was announced August 17, 2026. The rollout names NVIDIA A2000 compute, expanded sensors, cameras and redesigned storage/handles, and a fleet-learning World Model. Up to nine hours at a time differs from up to 18 operating hours per day. The October 2025 Thor announcement was an earlier plan, not proof that every shipped 2.0 unit uses IGX Thor. It transports clinical supplies rather than delivering patient care.

description: Ena is Enactic’s care-assistant humanoid program for routine support work such as tray handling, restocking, cleaning and laundry. The company advertises a beta planned for late 2026. These intended tasks and a foundation-model validation program do not establish full autonomous success rates, general commercial delivery or permission to perform clinical care. Development-support partnerships are not counts of deployed robots.
Modular embodied-AI robot that switches between dual-arm, bipedal and dual-wheel-leg configurations; launched December 2025 for research, education and prototyping with open APIs.
Wheeled dual-arm humanoid data-collection platform from Galaxea (星海图) with two 6-axis arms (70 cm reach), a two-finger gripper, an isomorphic teleoperation option and a working height of up to 1.7 m.
Bipedal humanoid from Galaxea (星海图), announced June 2, 2026, with joint torque above 130 N·m and several gripper options.
Humanoid from Stardust Intelligence (星尘智能) launched May 27, 2026, with automatic recharging, quick battery swaps and switching between scenarios.
Third-generation Kepler humanoid, first shown publicly at WAIC 2026 in Shanghai.
Wheeled variant of the Kepler K3 humanoid with telescoping arms, unveiled at WAIC 2026.
Foldable wheeled humanoid from RealMan (睿尔曼) shown at WAIC 2026. It can move sideways and its battery is rated for more than 12 hours.
Wheeled humanoid with a telescoping torso that gives 2.1 m of vertical working range, presented by RealMan at WAIC 2026.
Full-size tendon-driven humanoid (星仔) that ZTE launched Jul 18, 2026 for hospitality and public service.
Heavy-duty bipedal humanoid (星擎) launched by ZTE on Jul 18, 2026.
Industrial wheeled humanoid (星旺) for transport and inspection, launched by ZTE on Jul 18, 2026.
Humanoid from AI² Robotics (智平方) launched Sep 7, 2026, with whole-body coordination, force-controlled dual arms and an embodied foundation model.

Third-generation humanoid from Matrix Robotics (矩阵超智), launched January 2026. It has 3D-woven biomimetic sensing skin and a 27-DOF cable-driven 'Lingxi' hand, and has been deployed in a tennis venue serving drinks and collecting balls.
Wheeled embodied robot from Huichuan (汇川技术) launched Oct 12, 2026: a 7-axis arm on a mobile platform with full-body liquid cooling, IP54 protection and hot-swappable batteries.
Wheeled humanoid from cobot maker Elite Robots (艾利特), launched May 21, 2026, with an omnidirectional chassis.
Humanoid (小赛) from automaker Seres, introduced Jun 15, 2026, with variants for quality inspection and assembly-line work.

Low-cost bipedal humanoid from a Palo Alto startup, intended for home and healthcare assistance and driven by multimodal LLMs. The exterior was designed by Yves Behar/fuseproject. 1X Technologies later acquired the company.

Industrial 'superhumanoid' with two arms on an omnidirectional rover with four steerable wheels and up to 16 cameras. Used for truck loading/unloading, palletizing and order picking, and lifts boxes up to 8 ft high. One operator can supervise up to 10 units.

Wheeled dual-arm humanoid from a California startup for retail, logistics and assembly work. It learns tasks by imitation and runs onboard NVIDIA Jetson compute, with hot-swappable batteries and self-docking. Kinisi now redirects to Bear Robotics.

Toronto-based Stial's first humanoid, built for industrial polishing. It adjusts force, angle and trajectory in real time using 6D force sensing, after Stial's acquisition of the sensor maker STFcore. Its NextBrain AI combines force, touch, vision and hearing. It was introduced in February 2025.

Lightweight bipedal humanoid from Wuhan-based GLRoad (格蓝若), part of its 'Laborer' (劳动者) family, built for guided tours, exhibition halls and cultural-tourism interaction. It debuted at WRC 2026 and all of its parts are made in Hubei.

Full-size heavy-load bipedal humanoid from GLRoad's Laborer series. The maker bills it as the industry's first 50 kg-class heavy-payload humanoid. It has dual encoders on every joint and hardware-level safety redundancy. It was shown at the 2025 China International Supply Chain Expo.

Sichuan's first commercial full-size bipedal humanoid (天行者1号), released on 16 December 2024 by Chengdu-based Sichuan Embodied Humanoid Robot Technology (EIR). More than 90% of its core components are sourced locally.

Emotion-interaction humanoid (爱湫) with 59 degrees of freedom in its face. It recognizes at least 15 emotions and has a 360° microphone array. It was unveiled in Chengdu in December 2025 and went on sale at WRC 2026 in Interactive and Motion-Control editions.

Modular wheeled humanoid (nicknamed 'Xiaobai') from Blue Worm (蓝虫具身), a Xi'an Jiaotong University spin-out. Chassis, arms, waist and head attach through quick-connect interfaces. It has a 550 mm waist lift and teleoperation latency under 10 ms. Price starts at 9,800 CNY.

Small research-grade open-source humanoid with a near 1:1 mass-to-torque ratio and CAN-FD on every joint. It is marketed for sim-to-real in 24 hours and has competed at RoboCup and the World Humanoid Robot Games. Its global debut was at ICRA 2026.

Desktop-scale 12-DOF bipedal robot from HighTorque (高擎机电). It debuted at WAIC 2024, where it walked for three days without faults. The base version uses an RK3588 processor and a Pro version uses an Orin NX.

Small bipedal humanoid research platform for locomotion control, teaching and algorithm validation. It has a bionic human joint layout and supports CAN FD and secondary development. It debuted with Mini Pi at WAIC 2024.

Leju's general-purpose embodied-AI humanoid for scaled industrial use. It has quick-release hand and leg modules, battery swapping without downtime, 4 depth cameras plus 3D LiDAR, 100-2070 TOPS of configurable compute and a 400 N·m peak motor torque.

Wheeled version of Kuavo 5. It puts the humanoid upper body on a lifting wheeled chassis with a zero turning radius and an autonomously navigating base, aimed at long-shift indoor service and handling work.

Full-size bipedal humanoid from Beijing-based Zhongke Huiling (灵宝CASBOT). It has an optional 11-DOF dexterous hand, Orin AGX plus RK3588 compute (275 TOPS) and Wi-Fi 6/4G. An EDU edition adds LiDAR, navigation and wireless charging.

Wheeled dual-arm embodied-AI robot with a multi-stage lifting column that covers working heights from 0 to 2.1 m. It has 7-DOF arms with swappable grippers or dexterous hands, an IP68 rating and autonomous charging, and is aimed at warehouses, supermarkets and factories.

Wheeled humanoid from Spirit AI (千寻智能). It combines force-position hybrid 7-axis bionic arms with an omnidirectional chassis and has full-body STO safety. It runs the company's Spirit V1 VLA model for tasks such as folding clothes and tidying offices. It was officially released in June 2025.

Column-mounted half-body humanoid released in 2025 as the half-body module of Star L7. It uses two 12-active-DOF XHAND1 dexterous hands and 275 TOPS of compute, supports Meta Quest teleoperation and sorts parcels at China Post and SF Express hubs.

Full-size humanoid from industrial-robot maker ROKAE (珞石). It has full-joint force control with dual encoders, 6-DOF five-finger hands and a knee torque of at least 320 Nm, and integrates a VLA model for manufacturing, commercial and home work.

Heavy-duty wheeled dual-arm embodied 'AI worker' for factory handling, loading and unloading. It has an omnidirectional chassis, a 2-DOF head, dual six-axis force sensors and dual hot-swap batteries, and fits 0.8 m aisles. It was released in August 2026.

First general-purpose humanoid from Wuhan-based Guanggu Dongzhi (光谷东智). It is built for interactive service roles such as reception, showroom guiding and retail guidance, with multilingual voice, facial recognition, an expression screen and a swappable 700 Wh battery.

Foldable wheeled humanoid from Dongguan-based Tianji Robotics' Gento brand. It switches between 1700 mm unfolded and 790 mm folded to fit lifts and narrow doors. It has whole-body force control, 7-DOF arms, a 4WD/4WS omnidirectional base and Jetson Orin AGX, and debuted at ICRA 2026.

RoboScience's first robot: a wheeled humanoid with a lifting column and dual arms, running its Visics VLOA foundation model. It is 540 mm wide, enters 0.75 m aisles, reaches 0.1-2.0 m shelf heights and supports 5-second hot-swap battery changes.

Wheel-arm humanoid from Hefei-based Zerith (零次方). Its lifting column adjusts height from 130 to 180 cm and gives a 0-2.2 m reach. It has 7-DOF bionic arms, tactile arrays and the Zerith-V0 operation model, and is deployed for space cleaning and instant retail.

Bipedal humanoid from Hefei-based Zerith (零次方, a Tsinghua incubatee), released in October 2024. It has an 8-inch AMOLED face screen, a 6-microphone array, swappable batteries and more than 75% soft-material coverage.

Bipedal humanoid from Hangzhou's West Lake Robotics (西湖机器人), with modular 29-69 DOF configurations. It is driven by the West Lake University team's GAE general action pre-training model and targets performance, teaching and data collection.

Wheeled humanoid (巡霄) from Youibot's Tianyan series, released on 29 March 2025 with the Youibot-Xi'an Jiaotong University Embodied AI Institute. It is deployed for semiconductor Sub-FAB maintenance and power distribution room operation.
Full-size showroom-host humanoid from Chery's AiMOGA Robotics, with dexterous hands as standard. It greets visitors, serves drinks and opens car doors. It went on sale on JD.com in April 2026.

Wheeled embodied-AI humanoid (天兵一号) from Tianjin parallel-robot specialist Atom Robot (阿童木). It has a Stewart parallel waist, 7-DOF bionic arms, LiDAR plus stereo vision, 170 TOPS of edge AI compute and native ROS 2. It was released in December 2025.

Mid-size bipedal research humanoid (精灵3) from Shanghai-based BXI (半醒). It uses in-house hollow planetary joint motors and is capable of running, jumping and flips. It has a ROS2 SDK, MuJoCo simulation and hot-swappable batteries, and debuted at CES 2026.
Compact 132 cm humanoid that uses the same AI and perception stack as 4NE1 Gen 3. It is aimed at research, education and entertainment and comes in Standard and Pro (12-DoF dexterous hands) versions.

Bipedal version of Humanoid's HMND 01 Alpha industrial robot, unveiled in December 2025. It has 29 DoF (excluding end effectors), carries a 15 kg bimanual payload and runs the KinetIQ AI stack on NVIDIA compute.

Compact humanoid research platform built on NVIDIA GR00T and Jetson Thor, launched in October 2026 as the lab counterpart to the industrial Agile ONE. It has 71 DoF in total (31 body, 40 across two hands) and is scheduled to ship in early 2027.
Low-cost wheeled humanoid that combines two igus ReBeL cobot arms and bionic hands with the ReBeL Move AMR base. It navigates with LiDAR and 3D cameras, has a ROS2 interface and is CE certified.

handType: Interchangeable two-finger gripper, three-finger gripper or dexterous hand
description: Wheeled 'all-scene' embodied robot with in-house humanoid dual arms from Suzhou-based Zhijian Dynamics; the i7 was shown in April 2026 and the first 100 i7 Pro units were delivered on 6 July 2026, less than a year after the company was founded. Positioned as an out-of-the-box industrial robot deployable within a week, it handles long-horizon CNC machine tending (loading, clamping, unloading, inspection) with 0.1 mm-level positioning while moving between machines, using 360-degree sensor coverage and an automotive-grade electrical architecture.

size: Adjustable height 113-168 cm; base 57.5 x 35.6 cm
description: Indoor service humanoid officially named the AutoLife S3, made by Guangzhou-based AutoLife Robotics (Zhidong Weilai) and shown with a rainbow-gradient head at WRC 2026. It has 36 DoF on a Mecanum-wheel base, 7-DOF arms with 6-DOF dexterous hands, runs the company's '2AM' embodied brain with 'MINT' VLA motion model, reports about 99% grasp success, supports 80+ languages and low-latency teleoperation, and serves at Hong Kong's Wong Tai Sin Temple, Xi'an's Datang Everbright City and the 140th Canton Fair.

Humanoid robot for live-line testing in medium- and high-voltage substations and distribution rooms, custom-developed by Shenmou Technology for State Grid after it won a State Grid Hebei Electric Power tender in September 2025. It uses an electromagnetic-interference-resistant lightweight dexterous hand with modular tools to place sensors on test points, piezoelectric six-axis force sensing with force-position hybrid control, and multimodal AI for defect diagnosis; Shenmou reported it as the first humanoid delivered for this scenario in 2026.

China's first humanoid robot ('Pioneer'), built in 2000 by the robotics laboratory of the National University of Defense Technology in Changsha, achieving the country's first bipedal humanoid walking. Members of the same laboratory later developed China's first-generation quadruped bionic robot 'Tiema' and in 2026 founded the start-up Xiantu Qiyuan.

Electric bipedal humanoid in the 'Huitong' (BHR) line that Beijing Institute of Technology has developed over six generations since the early 2000s, commercialised by the BIT spin-off Ligong Huahui and updated with new in-house drive units at WRC 2023. The 2023 version is 165 cm tall, weighs 55 kg, has 26 degrees of freedom, runs at 7 km/h, jumps 0.5 m high and about 1 m forward from standing, climbs 20 cm stairs and steps over 30 cm obstacles.

Pair of life-size bionic humanoid news anchors named Xinyan and Xinyu, co-developed by Xinhua News Agency and UBTECH with director Zhang Yimou as lead appearance designer and unveiled on 5 November 2026 at the World Media Summit forum. They combine UBTECH's bionic skin, embodied hardware, operating system and emotion model with Xinhua's verified 'Xinhua Yudian' current-affairs agent for on-camera news reading and multilingual output, with planned use in study bases, city reception halls and overseas exchanges.

First humanoid robot from Ningbo-based PIA Automation (Junpu Intelligent), a subsidiary of Joyson Group, released at the end of 2023. It has 44 joints, walks at up to 7 km/h and can lift cartons, and was used in industrial settings for flexible tasks such as moving goods and machine loading and unloading.

Second-generation industrial humanoid from Joyson subsidiary PIA Automation, shown at the 2024 World Design Cities Conference in Shanghai with a metallic, mechanical styling aimed at factory use. The iterated version is 1.7 m tall with 12 degrees of freedom in its hands to identify and pick goods from shelves, and a 2025 multimodal upgrade added LLM and VLM models for multilingual dialogue, voice commands and vision-guided pick-and-place.

Wheeled humanoid robot from Dobot that premiered at the China International Industry Fair in September 2025 as part of its multi-form 'super factory' platform. It pairs dual high-precision arms with six-axis force sensing on an industrial chassis with a folding lift mechanism, ±10 mm chassis repeatability and passage through 500 mm gaps, and supports VR-based data collection.

Topstar's first humanoid robot (Xiaotuo), unveiled at its global open day in Dongguan on 12 September 2025. It rides on a four-steering-wheel base with 360-degree omnidirectional motion, runs a Zhipu AI large model, and uses 3D cameras and AI visual inspection to check injection-moulded parts and load trays; it had been validated in injection-moulding workshops.

Moby is a bipedal general-purpose humanoid robot from Noble Machines (formerly Under Control Robotics) of Sunnyvale, California, built for hazardous and physically demanding industrial work. The maker lists a 23 kg (50 lb) payload, 5-hour battery life, 0.8 m/s walking speed, stair and scaffolding mobility and teleoperation support; the company emerged from stealth in March 2026 with first units shipped to an industrial customer.

PR2 (Personal Robot 2) is a wheeled two-armed research robot developed by Willow Garage alongside the open-source ROS framework. It became available for purchase in September 2010 and carries stereo cameras, a Kinect, tilting Hokuyo laser scanners, fingertip pressure sensors and a telescoping spine; Willow Garage has since closed.

The Meka M1 is a wheeled humanoid mobile manipulation platform from Meka Robotics, released in 2011, with compliant series-elastic 7-DoF arms, 5-DoF hands, an expressive head and a holonomic base. It ran ROS on Ubuntu Linux and cost up to about 320,000 USD depending on configuration; Meka was acquired by Google in 2013.

Zeno is a small walking humanoid from Hanson Robotics, first shown in 2007, with an expressive Frubber skin face, face tracking and conversational AI. It was built as a human-robot interaction research platform, especially for autism spectrum disorder therapy, and has 36 degrees of freedom with HD cameras in its eyes.

BRUCE (Bipedal Robot Unit with Compliance Enhanced) is a kid-size open-platform humanoid for research and education, developed at UCLA's RoMeLa lab with Los Angeles-based Westwood Robotics and introduced in December 2022. It uses BEAR proprioceptive actuators for dynamic motion, has 16 DoF, stands 70 cm tall, weighs 4.8 kg and runs about 20 minutes of continuous dynamic motion; Westwood lists it at 15,290 USD.

TITAN is a dual-arm wheeled or tracked general-purpose robot from Milpitas, California-based RoboForce, launched in May 2025 for outdoor industrial work such as utility-scale solar construction, mining, manufacturing and inspection. The maker lists a 40 kg peak dual-arm payload, 1,100 mm arm reach, 1 mm manipulation precision, 1.5-2.1 m adjustable height and 8 hours runtime per battery pack.

ToddlerBot is a low-cost, fully 3D-printed open-source humanoid research platform from Stanford University (Shuran Song and C. Karen Liu's groups), published in 2025 for scalable policy learning and whole-body loco-manipulation. It stands 0.56 m tall, weighs 3.4 kg, has 30 active DoF, a Jetson Orin NX computer and stereo fisheye cameras, and can be built from commercial parts for under 6,000 USD.

Robonaut 2 (R2) is a dexterous humanoid developed by NASA Johnson Space Center with General Motors under a 2007 Space Act Agreement, revealed in February 2010 and launched to the International Space Station in 2011 as the first humanoid robot in space. It was initially deployed as a torso-only humanoid mounted on a stanchion; each 7-DoF arm can hold 20 lb in any pose in Earth gravity, and its arms move at up to 2 m/s.

BEAR (Battlefield Extraction-Assist Robot) is a prototype hydraulic humanoid torso on tracked legs developed by Vecna from 2004 to lift and carry wounded soldiers and heavy objects. It can lift 227 kg, stands 1.96 m tall, and combines teleoperation with cameras, laser range finders and joint force sensors; the project is inactive.

size: 500 x 510 mm base footprint, 600 mm torso lift
description: Feather is a bimanual wheeled humanoid platform from US startup Feather Robotics, sold from 2026 as open hardware for physical-AI developers. Two 7-DoF arms with 1 m reach sit on a torso with 600 mm vertical travel and a holonomic base reaching 1.3 m/s; it has 23 DoF, dual hot-swappable 48 V batteries for about 10 hours, swappable NVIDIA Jetson compute, a Zed stereo head camera and an open Python SDK, starting at 32,990 USD.

Roger is a rugged humanoid from San Francisco-based Minerva Humanoids for hazardous work such as oil and gas operations, condition monitoring, emergency response and remote explosive ordnance disposal, unveiled when the company emerged from stealth in October 2026. It is human-operated by design: the operator sees through Roger's cameras in a headset, body trackers drive its motion and haptic feedback returns contact information, and it weighs under 100 kg outfitted.

Alphabot G1 (also shown as Jingang G1) is a wheeled humanoid robot from CSJBot with a patented dual-column torso on a four-wheel-drive, four-wheel-steer base. Its arm carries up to 20 kg, it runs CSJBot's SmartStar large model for voice interaction, and it targets order picking and transfer between shelves; it was exhibited at the World Robot Conference (WRC) 2026 in Beijing in August 2026.

XMAN-L1 is a 136 cm compact humanoid robot from Shanghai-based KEENON Robotics, launched in May 2026 for reception, guidance and interactive entertainment in malls, restaurants and brand activations. It has 42 biomimetic degrees of freedom, knee joints with 132 Nm peak torque, more than 2,000 W of power per leg and up to 100 TOPS of onboard computing, and uses Doubao and Tencent large language models for conversation.

Aidol is a bipedal anthropomorphic AI robot from Moscow-based developer Aidol, presented in November 2025 as Russia's first AI humanoid (it fell on stage at the debut). It has 67 degrees of freedom including 14 per arm, an expressive face driven by 19 servos, two stereo cameras, runs its AI models fully offline, lifts up to 10 kg and walks at up to 6 km/h for up to six hours per charge; in April 2026 the company signed a supply contract for assistant robots with a Japanese customer.

Research humanoid developed by the Italian Institute of Technology (IIT) with the Italian workers' compensation authority INAIL as an evolution of iCub, designed with ergonomic geometry for physical human-robot collaboration such as shared lifting to reduce workers' musculoskeletal risk. It is 1.5 m tall, weighs 55.7 kg, carries loads of about 10 kg and has Wi-Fi 6E connectivity; it was demonstrated teleoperated from Italy at ICRA 2023 in London.

Open-source child-sized humanoid research platform for embodied AI, designed by the EU RobotCub consortium and built by the Italian Institute of Technology, able to crawl, walk, sit and manipulate objects. It has 53 degrees of freedom (9 per hand), cameras, microphones, force/torque sensors and whole-body tactile skin, runs the YARP middleware, and around 36 units had been built by 2017.

General-purpose humanoid robot from Geek+ built for warehouse work such as picking, box handling, packing and inspection, powered by the company's Geek+ Brain embodied AI model. Unveiled on 10 February 2026 and described by Geek+ as ready for mass production.

Wheeled lifting humanoid development platform from Gento (Tianji Robotics) for embodied-AI development and 24/7 engineering work, with whole-body force control, omnidirectional mobility and a lift mechanism giving continuous height adjustment from 785 to 1,695 mm. Launched on 11 August 2026 alongside the Gento Luna.

Dual-arm wheeled humanoid development platform from VLAI Robotics with 25 degrees of freedom, coordinated waist, head and arms, a four-wheel omnidirectional base and a VLA/world-model controller. Launched in August 2026 at a starting price of 19,800 CNY.

Industrial wheeled dual-arm embodied-AI robot from Boyin Hechuang, 1,730 mm tall, with two 7-DOF arms carrying 15 kg each (35 kg combined), ±0.05 mm repeatability and a 2 m/s top speed. It runs at least 8 hours and supports hot-swappable dual batteries with autonomous swapping in about 4 minutes; unveiled on 30 July 2026.

Wheeled humanoid robot from Longqi Robotics that pairs an industrial wheeled chassis with humanoid arms, offering 17 degrees of freedom (excluding end effectors and base), 5 kg per-arm payload, 80 kg chassis payload and 1.2 m/s speed. Unveiled at the China International Industry Fair in October 2026 for factory material delivery and handling.

Industrial self-evolving embodied-AI robot from Guangxiang Technology with a four-steer-wheel omnidirectional base, a lifting waist covering 0-2.5 m working height and two arms with 0.05 mm repeatability, totaling 27 force-controlled degrees of freedom. Launched in Beijing on 10 June 2026 for automotive and 3C production lines.

Small-size open humanoid platform from the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center (X-Humanoid), unveiled in August 2026 for research, education, guiding and performance use. The flagship version is 135 cm tall, weighs 39.5 kg, has 31 joints and a 2070 TFLOPS AI controller, and carries a depth camera, LiDAR and IMU; the robot is rated IP53.

Wheeled humanoid with dual arms and grippers from the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center (X-Humanoid), shown at the 2025 World Robot Conference. It is offered for guided tours, patrol and inspection with visible-light and thermal recognition, autonomous elevator riding via a VLA model, and VR teleoperation.

Full-size industrial bipedal humanoid unveiled by Dongguan-based Topstar at its TOPS DAY 2026 open day in November 2026. It is 172 cm tall, weighs 72 kg, has 7-axis humanoid arms with a cross-axis wrist and a 10 kg dual-arm payload for factory material handling and sorting; production timing and price have not been disclosed.

Wheeled humanoid robot 'Xiaotuo' from Topstar, launched in September 2025 as the company's first humanoid and validated in injection-molding workshops. It has two 7-DOF arms with 690 mm reach, a 2-DOF head, a 2-axis lifting/bending waist and an omnidirectional chassis, a 10 kg rated (20 kg max) payload, ±0.05 mm repeatability and an RGB-D camera.

Bench-mounted humanoid dual-arm robot from Topstar with two 7-DOF arms and a 2-DOF head carrying an RGB-D camera, microphones and speaker. It handles a 10 kg rated (20 kg max) payload per specification with ±0.03 mm repeatability and a 1 m/s maximum TCP speed.

Compact humanoid in the Lumen family from Wuhan-based Guanggu Dongzhi (HECBOT), launched in February 2026 for research and education, companionship, elder care and exhibitions. It is 1.3 m tall, weighs 35 kg, has more than 40 degrees of freedom, a 500 Wh battery for over 2 hours of operation, an Orin NX computer, LiDAR, stereo cameras, an expression screen and touch sensors.

Full-size running humanoid from the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center (X-Humanoid) that won the world's first humanoid half marathon in Beijing Yizhuang in April 2025 in 2:40:42. It is about 180 cm tall and 55 kg, uses high-power integrated joints, low-inertia legs, UWB-guided autonomous navigation and hot-swappable batteries, and later set 100 m sprint records at the 2026 World Humanoid Robot Games.

Fourth-generation wheel-legged humanoid from GAC Group's incubated robotics spin-off Huilun Technology (慧仑科技), publicly announced by GAC chairman Feng Xingya in October 2025. By August 2026 (WRC 2026) nearly 50 units were deployed across Guangzhou, Hong Kong, Xiamen and Tianjin for car-plant line inspection, park/metro security patrol and guiding. It switches between wheel-leg modes, recovers from falls, and at WRC 2026 showed a tri-fold transport configuration and an on-site water-spray test.

First consumer home-companion humanoid from Chery's AiMOGA (Moga Technology), shown at WRC 2026 and launched with global pre-orders on 21 October 2026 in Wuhu. It uses the in-house MoAgent model for voice interaction, visual object recognition, schedule reminders and long-term memory, with volume production planned for the end of 2026.

Humanoid robot developed in-house by Dongfeng Motor's R&D institute in Wuhan, shown in November 2025 with a DF30 automotive-grade MCU, a 700+ TOPS Tianyuan T500 controller and an on-board 8B multimodal model. An upgraded version with dexterous hands appeared at WRC 2026; Dongfeng plans factory training for sorting, handling and quality inspection from late 2026 and small-batch production in 2027.

Full-size bipedal humanoid from Wuhan-based Hubei Jingchu Humanoid Robot Co., a company with a core team from Huazhong University of Science and Technology. It is about 170 cm tall, is driven by planetary roller-screw linear actuators, and integrates voice interaction, autonomous navigation and a large language model for teaching, equipment monitoring and interactive entertainment.

Industrial bipedal humanoid from Hubei Jingchu Humanoid Robot Co. that uses planetary roller-screw linear drives throughout the body. It is about 175 cm tall and is aimed at handling, assembly and inspection; in 2025 it was trained for parts sorting in a factory before deployment.

Wheeled service robot ('Jingchu Elf') from Hubei Jingchu Humanoid Robot Co. for hotel reception, mall guiding and showroom sales. It is about 160 cm tall, weighs 80 kg, uses LiDAR, a depth camera and SLAM navigation for autonomous guiding, supports face recognition and runs the Qwen large language model for conversation, with about 8 hours of operation.

Smallest member of Hubei Jingchu Humanoid Robot Co.'s Jingchu family, released in September 2025 for education, entertainment and home companionship of children and elderly people. It uses rotary joint modules with compliant control, an AI voice kit, five-finger dexterous hands and stereo depth cameras for autonomous navigation.

Humanoid robot series developed by Academician Liu Sheng's team at Wuhan University and first shown in Hubei's 'Chucai' humanoid showcase in February 2025 with 38 degrees of freedom and 7-DOF dexterous hands. The third generation is 1.65 m tall, runs at up to 5 m/s (100 m in about 20 s), has bionic tactile feet and about 80% Hubei-made core parts; it targets elderly care and medical services.

'Worker No. 1' (Laodongzhe) humanoid developed by Academician Chen Xuedong's team at Huazhong University of Science and Technology with Wuhan Gelanruo Precision Technology, shown in Wuhan in November 2024. The Laodongzhe series is 1.8 m tall, weighs 95 kg and can lift about 50 kg; it is intended for substation inspection and maintenance pilots.

Bipedal humanoid that originated in Academician Ding Han's team at Huazhong University of Science and Technology, shown in Hubei's 'Chucai' showcase in February 2025 and released as a production model by Hubei Qiling Robot in November 2025. The production version is 1.75 m tall, weighs 55 kg, has 43 movable joints driven by in-house high-torque-density motors, resists push disturbances, and uses stereo vision with LiDAR for autonomous navigation in teaching, guiding and factory logistics.

Humanoid robot series from Wuhan Guanggu Huahui Technology, founded in Wuhan by Professor Huang Qiang's Beijing Institute of Technology team, shown in Hubei's 'Chucai' showcase in February 2025. It uses in-house joints and aerospace-derived materials, can walk, run, jump, roll and stand up again after falls, and targets public security, border patrol and firefighting tasks.

Fifth-generation Gongga humanoid unveiled by the Chengdu Humanoid Robot Innovation Center on 11 November 2026 and aimed at household tasks. Its in-house embodied-AI stack fuses RGB, depth and pose data into a 3D scene graph, keeps a long-term spatio-temporal memory of objects across days, uses causal task planning with re-planning, and a latent action-conditioned world model to rehearse grasping, tidying and wiping before acting.

Panda-styled humanoid robot developed by Chengdu Xingjin Humanoid Robot Technology, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Chengdu Humanoid Robot Innovation Center, and unveiled at the Chengdu People's Congress in January 2026. It is 1.52 m tall with 21 degrees of freedom, walks with straight knees at speed, talks in several languages and Sichuan dialect, and is offered for guiding, performances and factory inspection.

Second-generation wheeled humanoid from Chengdu industrial-robot maker CRP (Kanop), first shown publicly in March 2026. It combines a wheeled base with a humanoid upper body, has 33 actuated joints with sub-millimetre motion control, and targets inspection, sorting and handling in factories, ports and warehouses, with volume production planned for the second half of 2026.

Full-size industrial humanoid for hazardous special-operations work from Tianjin-based Shiyun Technology; the first batch of 15 units rolled off the line in Tianjin's Hexi district in August 2026. It is 174 cm tall, weighs 55 kg, runs about 8 hours with 10-second hot-swap batteries, handles steps, slopes and rough ground, and targets power inspection, security, equipment maintenance and rail inspection, with scale deliveries planned for 2027.

Health-care companion humanoid launched in Changsha in January 2025 by Hunan Chaoneng Robot Technology, a company spun out of the National University of Defense Technology. It integrates a medical large model developed with Xiangya School of Medicine and is designed for vital-sign checks, massage and rehabilitation exercises, helping users get up, turn over and move, and entertainment such as dancing and piano playing.

Home general-purpose wheeled humanoid from Beijing-based GigaAI (Jijia Shijie), launched in Wuhan's Optics Valley in May 2026 with the Hubei Humanoid Robot Innovation Center under the SeeLight home sub-brand. Driven by GigaAI's embodied foundation models rather than preset rules, it folds clothes, heats meals in a microwave, clears tables and loads dishes; a 100-unit order was placed for trials in real homes.

Fully domestically sourced full-size special-purpose humanoid developed by China North Industries Group's (Norinco) Intelligent Innovation Research Institute and shown at WRC 2026. It is designed for sentry duty with person recognition and anomaly alerts, all-weather patrol and hazardous-area work, operates in coordinated formations and can mirror an operator's movements in real time via the 'Avatar' teleoperation system built for 90 kg-class full-size humanoids.

Electric-power work humanoid developed in-house by China Southern Power Grid's Guangdong Power Grid robotics lab, first shown at the 2024 China Hi-Tech Fair. By November 2025 it operated autonomously instead of by remote control, performing 11 trained tasks such as opening switchgear doors, pressing buttons, turning knobs and switching operations, and walking on grass and cobblestones in substations.

Bipedal humanoid from Changsha construction-machinery maker Zoomlion and its AI subsidiary Zhongke Yungu, shown at Hannover Messe and KOMATEK 2026 and at WRC 2026. It is designed for industrial collaboration, guiding and education; demonstrations include imitation-learned wire-harness gripping and bundling, Tai Chi, face recognition, voice dialogue, autonomous navigation and multi-robot coordinated dancing.

Wheeled humanoid from Zoomlion's Zhongke Yungu robotics unit, shown at WRC 2026 working alongside logistics robots. It performs unstructured grasping and sorting of irregular items and precision assembly steps such as pre-fitting car mirrors, and is part of Zoomlion's in-house humanoid line deployed in its Changsha smart factories.

Industrial-grade wheeled dual-arm embodied robot launched in December 2025 by Shanghai STEP Electric, the industrial-robot subsidiary of Haier Group. It offers 3, 5 or 10 kg dual-arm payload options with dexterous hands or grippers, ±180° upper-body rotation, a 0-61 cm waist lift for a 0-210 cm working height, a four-wheel chassis with 3D LiDAR, and autonomous hot-swap battery exchange for 24/7 operation.

First-generation wheeled industrial humanoid in Midea Group's 'Meiluo' (MIRO) series, deployed in May 2025 at Midea's Jingzhou washing-machine factory. Scheduled by the factory's central control system, it performs 3D quality inspection, equipment patrols and sheet-metal loading.

Commercial and home service humanoid series ('Meila') from Midea Group, shown in 2025 alongside its industrial MIRO robots. It can take items from a fridge, heat food in a microwave and brew coffee with a coffee machine, and Midea planned to place it in its retail experience stores in 2026 for guiding and appliance demonstrations.

Hisense's first commercial humanoid robot, unveiled at CES 2026, positioned as a service humanoid for greeting visitors and acting as a sales guide. It holds multilingual conversations, leads exhibition tours and uses Hisense's in-house Xinghai large model and appliance knowledge base to explain product specifications, check stock and suggest purchases, with deployment planned first in Hisense stores.

Household butler robot from Qingdao-based Hisense, shown at AWE 2026, with a humanoid upper body on a wheeled base. It fetches and places items, operates household appliances, helps with laundry and food preparation, and acts as a mobile hub that coordinates Hisense smart appliances.

Bipedal humanoid from Wuhu-based Qizhi Robotics, a company set up by industrial-robot maker Efort with the national advanced manufacturing fund and Wuhu Science and Technology Group, unveiled in February 2025 as Wuhu's first humanoid. It runs the Openmind OS general robot software base developed by Efort and Qizhi, with 3D spatial perception, dexterous manipulation and interactive task understanding.

Wheeled humanoid from Wuhu-based Qizhi Robotics (an Efort joint venture), unveiled alongside the bipedal Yobot R1 in February 2025. It pairs a humanoid upper body with an impact-resistant wheeled base and runs the Openmind OS robot software base for perception, manipulation and human interaction, demonstrated serving water and porridge.

Next-generation home general-purpose wheeled humanoid announced by Beijing-based GigaAI (Jijia Shijie) as the successor to the SeeLight S1. GigaAI states it is a system-level redesign with a 60% smaller chassis, 70% longer runtime and a working height of up to 2.2 m for small homes, with founder-edition reservations for real households.

Mobile two-arm research robot from Beijing-based ARX Robotics (方舟无限) that mounts two 6-DOF X5 arms with grippers on a lifting column (about 0-380 mm travel) over an omnidirectional-wheel base. It carries RTX 5070 compute, uses hot-swappable battery packs and is programmed in Python on Ubuntu 24.04 for mobile-manipulation and demonstration-data collection.

Wheeled humanoid with two arms and a sensor head from ARX Robotics (方舟无限), introduced in August 2024 as a mobile platform for embodied-AI research and imitation learning; ARX publishes ROS 2 and imitation-learning SDKs for the X7s version.

Modular wheeled dual-arm general-purpose robot from Dexmal (原力灵机), unveiled at its Action 2026 developer conference on 9 July 2026 to run the company's DM0.5 embodied foundation model. Each 1 m arm carries 3 kg with hot-swappable end-effectors, the head has dual fisheye cameras for 360-degree vision, the omnidirectional chassis uses two Hesai JT LiDARs, and batteries can be swapped in 30 seconds without shutting down the controller.

handType: Quick-change tools (electric wrench, vacuum cup, gripper)
description: First humanoid robot from industrial-robot maker YiFei Technology (翼菲科技), unveiled on 17 November 2025. It pairs two 7-DOF bionic arms (0.6 m reach, 5 kg peak payload, ±0.05 mm repeatability) with a modular four-wheel-steer omnidirectional base that has a 0.5 m lifting column, runs the company's YiBrain multimodal model and swaps tools for screw driving, cable insertion and labeling.

Wheeled logistics humanoid series from forklift maker Hangcha Group (杭叉集团), unveiled at CeMAT ASIA 2025 in Shanghai on 28 October 2025. It combines a self-developed AMR chassis with a humanoid upper body whose two arms have 14 degrees of freedom, and handles case and tote transfer, palletizing and depalletizing; Hangcha said it was in small-batch pilot use with volume sales planned for 2026.

size: 180 cm tall; 490 x 650 x 1800 mm packed
description: Mobile lifting dual-arm robot from DISCOVER Robotics (求之科技), a Tsinghua AIR spin-off based in Wuxi, launched for global pre-sale in July 2024. Two 6-DOF AIRBOT Play arms ride a lift with 0.91 m travel on a differential-drive base, with a 2-DOF head carrying a RealSense D435i camera, a chassis LiDAR for autonomous navigation and exoskeleton-backpack or VR teleoperation for data collection.

Flagship wheeled dual-arm humanoid from Galaxea AI (星海图) launched at the World Robot Conference in Beijing in August 2026. It has 30 degrees of freedom across arms, neck, waist and base with force-position control, a combined arm payload of up to 20 kg and 8-hour runtime with fast charging, battery swap or autonomous recharging, aimed at e-commerce, manufacturing, logistics and commercial service.

Industrial humanoid from Huashu Robot (华数机器人) that mounts a humanoid upper body on a mobile base, announced in August 2026 ahead of market launch. It has 23 degrees of freedom, 10 kg payload per arm, 738 mm arm reach, force control, depth vision and exchangeable end tools for precision assembly, material sorting and workshop inspection.

Wheeled humanoid from Shenzhen Cyborg Robot Technology (赛博格机器人), launched at the China Hi-Tech Fair in November 2025 together with its Cyborg-H02 hand. Its base turns on the spot, reaches 1 m/s with ±1 cm navigation accuracy and passes 0.75 m aisles; it is used for factory material picking and SMT line loading with MES/WMS integration.

Wheeled humanoid from GigaAI (极佳视界) unveiled on 26 November 2025 as a native body for its physical-AI models. It is 1.62 m tall, weighs 88 kg, has 28 degrees of freedom and a 3 kg rated (5 kg maximum) payload per arm, with RGB-D cameras on head, chest and hands plus chassis LiDAR and ultrasonic sensors.

Lifting-column embodied-AI robot (纪灵-S1) from Zhongke Diwuji (中科第五纪), launched at the China International Industry Fair on 12 October 2026 together with the company's new embodied brain model. It has 19 degrees of freedom, a lifting column and 360-degree waist rotation for a working envelope about 2.8 m in diameter, 5 kg payload per arm, force control and quick-change end tools for precision assembly, flexible production lines and warehouse sorting.

Wheeled dual-arm restocking robot from Zhengxing Innovation (正行创新) launched on 8 October 2026 for convenience stores and supermarkets. Its 7-DOF arms carry 3 kg each, a 920 mm lift covers working heights of about 100-1,750 mm, the narrow omnidirectional base passes aisles under 600 mm, and it has 2,070 TFLOPS of compute, about 6 hours of runtime and battery swap or autonomous recharging.

Bipedal service humanoid from Zhengxing Innovation (正行创新) launched on 8 October 2026 for retail and public spaces. It is 1.4 m tall with 26 degrees of freedom, 2 m/s top speed, 157 TOPS of compute, support for more than 20 languages with 45 expressions and 36 gestures, and open ROS and SDK interfaces.

Wheeled dual-arm humanoid development edition from Tianchuang Robot (天创机器人), launched in July 2026 at 23,900 CNY. It can be used on a fixed or mobile base, takes 5-DOF or 7-DOF arms with 3 kg payload and 740 mm reach each, and includes an onboard compute module for embodied-AI development.

Wheeled humanoid from the Suzhi series of Shenzhen Haoling Robotics (壕翎机器人), a subsidiary of automation supplier Haosen Intelligent (豪森智能), launched on 18 August 2026 and positioned as an industrial embodied-AI assembly robot for unstructured factory tasks.

Wheel-arm embodied-AI robot from Huibo Robotics (汇博机器人) launched on 13 August 2026, integrating a wheeled base with humanoid dual arms. It navigates autonomously to work points and is aimed at inspection, handling, assembly, commercial service and teaching and research.

Heavy-duty dual-arm humanoid from JAKA Robotics (节卡) premiered at WAIC 2026. Each arm weighs under 30 kg yet carries 30 kg (50 kg with both arms) using JAKA's APEX high-torque planetary joints, and it can be mounted on a micron-level positioning base to form a Kargo wheeled humanoid for tasks such as motor assembly screw fastening.

Heavy-payload wheeled humanoid from JAKA Robotics (节卡) launched at the China International Industry Fair in October 2026 as an upgrade of the factory-proven JAKA Kargo, extending its mobile manipulation to higher-payload industrial tasks.

Industrial-native humanoid (隙锋) from Youibot (优艾智合) launched on 29 June 2026 as part of its Tianyan humanoid series together with the FabriX industrial embodied model. Youibot says it ships with basic skills and reaches about 90% task success after around 50 on-site demonstrations, retraining on a 24-hour cycle and coordinating with other robots under a one-brain, multi-body architecture.

Heavy-duty two-wheel-legged humanoid from Lanyue Dynamics (揽月动力), launched on 23 June 2026. It uses reduced-order-model whole-body control at up to 1,000 Hz, can carry a 20 kg tote up a slope and clamp-lift 20 kg to 1.8 m for industrial palletizing and line feeding.

Humanoid-arm mobile robot nicknamed 'Optimus' (擎天柱) from forklift maker EP Equipment (中力股份), launched at the company's 629 event on 29-30 June 2026 alongside its UHX-01 and XORD1 arm-type robots as part of a new embodied mobile-manipulation series.

Wheeled humanoid (逐星H1) from industrial and collaborative robot maker ROKAE (珞石), shown at the World Robot Conference in August 2026. It has 23 degrees of freedom, an omnidirectional base, two 7-axis Taibai AR force-controlled humanoid arms and ROKAE's iNex motion controller with whole-body control; five units handle tote transport, part picking, press-fitting and screw assembly at Schaeffler's Taicang plant.

Industrial wheeled embodied robot (大白机器人2.0) from Beijing startup Puluo Yuzhou (普罗宇宙), launched on 1 November 2025 as a successor to the August 2025 original with upgrades to over 300 performance points. It offers ±0.05 mm absolute positioning, MES integration, a humanoid upper body with modular end effectors for screw locking, soldering, dispensing and oiling, and a separable base and body; it is sold online through JD.com.

Wheeled embodied-AI robot series (黑豹) from UniX AI (优理奇) launched in February 2026 as the successor to Wanda 2.0. It pairs production-grade 8-DOF bionic arms and adaptive grippers with an omnidirectional four-wheel-steer, four-wheel-drive base, an upper body that lifts through 80 cm for floor-to-shelf work and a 48 V power platform, and is piloted in elder care, retail, catering and hotel services.

Full-size bipedal humanoid in the NAVIAI ('Navigator') family from the Ningbo-based Zhejiang Humanoid Robot Innovation Center, presented in November 2025 as a security-patrol 'mechanical guardian'. It is 180 cm tall, walks and runs at up to 9 km/h, carries 25 kg, and has a 3-DOF waist and joints with up to 360 N·m peak torque for security inspection and research use.

Wheeled dual-arm humanoid from the Zhejiang Humanoid Robot Innovation Center, introduced in 2026 as the newer model after the NAVIAI-WA1 and described by the company as its main volume product. It has upgraded 8-DOF humanoid arms with ±0.02 mm end repeatability and runs about 6 hours per charge with roughly 2 hours of charging; it targets handling and sorting, precision assembly and garment manufacturing, and was demonstrated in logistics with KION at LogiMAT 2026.

Bipedal industrial humanoid 'Suyuan' developed in-house by Shanghai Electric and launched in August 2025 for inspection, picking, handling and assembly. The launch version is 1.67 m tall, weighs 50 kg, has 38 degrees of freedom, a 2 kg single-arm and 10 kg total load, walks at 5 km/h and uses LiDAR, stereo cameras and a 275 TOPS on-board computer; an upgraded version shown at WAIC 2026 has 41 degrees of freedom and hot-swappable dual batteries.

Industrial wheeled pan-humanoid robot 'Tuoyuan' from Shanghai Electric, shown at WAIC 2026. Using an embodied large model and force-position hybrid control, it plugs and unplugs USB, aviation and DC power connectors in cabinets while tidying cables, sorts mixed bolts into bins, and loads and unloads automotive sheet-metal parts.

Bionic wheeled pan-humanoid robot 'Mermaid' from Shanghai Electric for electrical operating tasks, shown at WAIC 2026. It recognises buttons, knobs, push-type panel locks and air circuit breakers without prior teaching, generates compliant operating paths in real time, and uses compliant force control to operate electrical cabinets without damaging components.

Full-size electric bipedal humanoid from China Electronics Technology Group's 21st Research Institute and CETC Robotics in Shanghai, launched as 'Tansuo D1' at the small-motor technology exhibition in Shanghai in November 2025. It weighs 75 kg, runs at up to 10 km/h, jumps about 0.5 m forward and 20 cm high, handles 20 cm steps and 20-degree slopes, has sealed waterproof, dustproof and corrosion-resistant joints, fingertip pressure sensors with 0.1 N sensitivity and autonomous charging, and targets logistics, manufacturing and special operations.

Bipedal humanoid welding robot from Changsha-based Hunan Shibit Robot, launched in November 2026 for welding in shipyard hull compartments, with shipyard trials planned from the end of 2026. It has 27 degrees of freedom, a 10 kg arm and 30 kg whole-body payload, a LiDAR and three ToF cameras for mapping and navigation, and a wrist-mounted 3D line-scan camera for millimetre-level seam location, and can squat and half-kneel for flat, vertical and overhead welds in 55-60 °C conditions.

Centaur-style wheel-legged robot from Shanghai Runke Juneng Technology, a company founded in 2025 and jointly held by Runyang Technology and Fourier, first shown in July 2026. It pairs a four-wheel-leg base with two humanoid arms in an explosion-proof design for reconnaissance, inspection and handling in nuclear, emergency, mining, oilfield and steel-plant settings, and carries 100-120 kg on average (210 kg static peak); the upgraded version at WRC 2026 climbed 60 cm obstacles.

First-generation 'Gongga' ultra-lightweight humanoid from the Chengdu Humanoid Robot Innovation Center, unveiled on 28 October 2024. It weighs 25 kg, carries up to 5.5 kg and runs up to 8 hours; its full-stack in-house AI interprets task intent, observes the environment and generates task flows to control its limbs, and about 60% of its parts come from Chengdu suppliers.

Full-size high-performance humanoid robot from MirrorMe Technology (Mirror Me), unveiled in February 2026 as the fastest humanoid on the ground, with a peak running speed above 11 m/s. It stands 175 cm tall, weighs 75 kg and has a 50 kg payload capacity, using whole-body dynamics and human-proportioned bionic design.

The W1, introduced as Hobbs W1 in December 2025, is a wheeled service humanoid from Beijing-based Noetix Robotics that combines a hyper-realistic bionic head (32 active and 8 passive degrees of freedom) with two 5-DoF arms, 6-DoF dexterous hands and a mobile base. It is aimed at scenic-spot guiding, corporate reception, university tours and hospital guidance; each arm weighs 3.3 kg and carries 2 kg.

handType: dexterous hands with adaptive soft grippers
description: Orca I is a bipedal humanoid from Shanghai-based Cyan Robotics (Qingxin Yichuang) focused on emotional interaction, with straight-knee walking, an emotion-expressing face display and an emotion-gait model, plus a large language model for conversation. It stands 151 cm tall, weighs about 42 kg with batteries, has 28 degrees of freedom, carries about 5 kg per arm (10 kg with both) and runs about 2 hours standing or 1 hour walking on two swappable batteries.

Xingxingxia P2 (Star Ranger P2) is a dual-form service humanoid from Shenzhen-based Digital Huaxia, launched in May 2026, that switches between a bipedal walking mode and a wheeled mode and docks itself for recharging. It is about 130 cm tall, weighs about 39 kg, has 30+ degrees of freedom and carries up to 3 kg, with about 2 hours of runtime walking and 8 hours in wheeled mode; flagship (38 DoF, lidar, omnidirectional base), standard (30 DoF) and basic (25 DoF) versions target government halls, banks and tourism venues with 20+ languages.

Xialan R03 is a hyper-realistic bionic humanoid from Shenzhen-based Digital Huaxia, released in July 2026 for unattended reception, guided tours and customer service. It has an expressive face with 23 active and 40+ passive degrees of freedom supporting 30+ expressions, 4-DoF arms, a rotating waist and wake-word-free full-duplex multilingual conversation, and is mounted on a desk or pillar at an adjustable 160-170 cm height.

Xiaoman (M-Series) is a high-payload wheeled lifting humanoid robot from Beijing Changxing Power Robot Technology, a subsidiary of Xinxing Equipment, aimed at industrial handling and assembly, elderly care and special operations. Its dual arms lift up to 100 kg, its working height adjusts from 0 to 2.2 m, it has 23 active degrees of freedom, weighs about 483 kg and runs 4-5 hours per 3-hour charge with autonomous navigation and voice interaction; the current version 2.0 is listed as in development.

Vbot ATOM is a bipedal humanoid from Beijing-based Vbot (Vita Dynamics) designed for living spaces such as homes, retail, hotels and offices, unveiled with pre-orders opening at the 2026 World Robot Conference. It is 160 cm tall with a 180 cm arm span and 95 cm leg length, has 31 degrees of freedom, a face display with ear lights, full-body fabric covering and quiet footpads.

RP1 (ROBOTO 01) is a full-stack open-source bipedal humanoid from Shanghai RoboParty (founded by Huang Yi), shown at IROS 2026 in Pittsburgh and formally released on X on October 14, 2026, as the flagship successor to the company's ROBOTO Origin DIY project. It publishes mechanical CAD, PCB, firmware, SDK and training tools on GitHub, is 1.35 m tall with 24 active degrees of freedom (30 in the Pro version), in-house ROMOMO joints with up to 160 Nm peak torque on some joints, a top running speed of 4 m/s, and a modular head, dexterous hand and end-effector.

KaiBot (KAI) is a full-size, highly anthropomorphic humanoid robot from Shenzhen-based Kinetix AI (Chaowei Dongli), unveiled in April 2026 for home and service use. It is 173 cm tall, weighs 70 kg and has about 115 degrees of freedom including two 36-DoF dexterous hands, tactile skin with 18,000 sensing points, a 20 kg load capacity, a top speed of 5 km/h and about four hours of runtime from a 1.7 kWh semi-solid-state battery; the company targets a price under 40,000 USD.

Tiangong (later called Tiangong 1.0 Lite) is the first general-purpose humanoid robot platform from the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center (X-Humanoid), launched in April 2024 as an open, extensible reference body for embodied-AI research. It is 163 cm tall, weighs 43 kg, has 550 trillion operations per second of onboard compute, six-axis force sensors, an IMU and 3D vision, and was presented as the first full-size all-electric humanoid to run in a humanlike way at 6 km/h.

Tiangong 1.1 Pro is an August 2024 iteration of the Tiangong humanoid from the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center (X-Humanoid) that added complete functional arms to the research platform. It is 163 cm tall, weighs 56 kg, has 42 degrees of freedom, multiple vision sensors, six-axis force sensors, an IMU, 3D vision and 550 trillion operations per second of compute.

Tiangong 1.2 Max is a full-size embodied-AI humanoid from the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center (X-Humanoid), released in August 2024 and used in the 2024 World Robot Conference opening ceremony to carry and place the conference emblem autonomously. It is 173 cm tall, weighs 60 kg and has 320 Nm hip and knee joint torque, with higher payload, speed and endurance than Tiangong 1.1 Pro.

Tianyi is a wheeled embodied-AI service humanoid from the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center (X-Humanoid), launched in August 2024 for reception, guided tours, Q&A and performances. It is 163 cm tall, weighs 72.5 kg, has 16 degrees of freedom, an omnidirectional wheeled base with height-adjustable legs, two arms and a chest screen, and an emotion model co-developed with Peking University to recognise facial expressions.

CASBOT W2 is a wheeled dual-arm embodied-AI robot from Beijing CASBOT (Zhongke Huiling) for industrial manufacturing, mining and energy, and data-collection factories, launched at the company's ecosystem partner conference in April 2026 and shown at the 2026 World Robot Conference. It combines a wheeled mobile base with two arms and 27 degrees of freedom and covers a vertical working range of 0 to 2 m.

CASBOT Mini is a half-size humanoid robot from Beijing CASBOT (Zhongke Huiling) for education, research and developers, launched in April 2026 with open expansion capabilities. It opened a limited pre-sale at 29,900 CNY, and the first 50 units sold out at the launch event.

CASBOT 02 Lite is a full-size humanoid secondary-development platform from Beijing CASBOT (Zhongke Huiling) based on the CASBOT 02, shown at the 2026 World Robot Conference. It is 163 cm tall, weighs 40 kg, has 23 degrees of freedom, supports high-dynamic dance motions and carries an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin module, with open hardware and software interfaces, SDK and documentation.

Xingzhe 2 (Walker II) is a full-size bipedal humanoid from Shanghai DroidUp (Zhuoyide) built around the company's bionic tendon-and-cable drive, with a lightweight high-strength body. It took third place in the April 2025 Beijing E-Town humanoid robot half marathon and was exhibited and performed at the 2025 World Robot Conference and World Humanoid Robot Games.

Approximately 3 ft (91 cm), 35 lb bipedal humanoid from StarBot Robotics of Santa Barbara, California, intended for robotics education, programming practice and AI projects, with 22 degrees of freedom and a 24 V battery rated for up to 3 hours. Released September 2026 and on sale from October 18, 2026 starting at 7,999 USD (5,999 USD for the first 100 orders).

5 ft (152 cm), 75 lb bipedal humanoid research platform from StarBot Robotics with 23 full-body degrees of freedom and a 48 V battery, aimed at universities and R&D teams working on motion control, reinforcement learning and sim-to-real transfer. Released July 2026 from 9,999 USD; top speed listed at 3 m/s.

ADA-7 is a wheeled social/service humanoid robot made by Turkish manufacturer AKINROBOTICS (a subsidiary of AKINSOFT), the latest member of the ADA series used for education, retail, tourism and healthcare settings. It stands 166cm tall, weighs 65kg, has an LED face display and a 10.1-inch touchscreen, supports 15+ languages, and offers autonomous charging and autonomous navigation.

Mini ADA is a compact wheeled social humanoid robot by Turkish maker AKINROBOTICS, positioned as a smaller companion to the ADA-7 for education, retail, entertainment and healthcare use. It is 123cm tall, weighs 45kg, has an LED face and 10.1-inch screen, supports 15+ languages, and offers optional autonomous charging.

AKINCI is a wheeled humanoid robot developed by Turkish manufacturer AKINROBOTICS, with AKINCI-5 the current generation of the ongoing project series. Earlier AKINCI-4 weighed 48kg, stood 150cm tall, ran on a lithium-ion battery for about 5 hours, and supported Turkish, English, Russian and Arabic; AKINROBOTICS markets AKINCI-5 for exhibitions, education and corporate reception use.

SURALP (Sabanci University Robot Research Laboratory Platform) is a bipedal humanoid research robot built by Sabanci University in Istanbul, Turkey, unveiled in 2010 after eight years of development costing about 1 million USD. It stands 164cm tall, weighs 114kg, and has 29 degrees of freedom (12 in the legs, 12 in the arms, 2 in the neck and 1 in the torso); at its debut it danced, answered yes/no questions and walked up an inclined ramp.

4NE1 Gen 4 is the fourth generation of NEURA Robotics' general-purpose humanoid robot, developed and built in Germany. It introduces a slimmer design with a sensorized textile outer skin about 20% lighter than the previous generation, upgraded dexterous hands for more precise grip, and limbs with local reflex responses, all running on NEURA's multimodal Neuron AI foundation model processed onboard. As of late 2026 it is operating in NEURA's Gym training facilities and being prepared for series production.

The X1 is a small-scale open-source humanoid robot from AGIBOT (Zhiyuan Robotics), positioned as a full-stack, modular research platform. It stands 130 cm tall, weighs 33 kg, and has 34 active degrees of freedom with proprietary PowerFlow actuators and an OmniPicker gripper.

T-HR3 is Toyota's third-generation humanoid robot, unveiled in November 2017, standing 1.5 m tall and weighing 75 kg with 32 torque-controlled joints and a pair of 10-fingered hands. It is operated remotely through Toyota's Master Maneuvering System, a wearable master-arm and master-foot rig with a head-mounted display that lets an operator's movements be mirrored by the robot, including a 2018 demonstration of 5G remote control with NTT DOCOMO.

EMIEW (Excellent Mobility and Interactive Existence as Workmate) is a bipedal humanoid service robot developed by Hitachi, first unveiled in 2005, standing 130 cm tall, weighing 70 kg, with 14 degrees of freedom and a top speed of 6 km/h. It was designed for office guidance and communication tasks and was followed by the smaller EMIEW 2 and EMIEW3 successors.

Cinnamon 2 is a bipedal humanoid robot from Japanese startup Donut Robotics, marketed as the world's first mass-produced gesture-controlled biped and built on the company's own Japanese vision-language-action (VLA) model. Initial units are built on a China-sourced hardware base around 130 cm tall while Donut Robotics works toward a fully domestic-made version, with the robot unveiled at SusHi Tech Tokyo 2026 and later positioned for eldercare-support deployments through a 2026 partnership with Charm Care Corporation.

NEXTAGE Fillie OPEN is Kawada Robotics' ROS-compatible research platform variant of its NEXTAGE Fillie dual-arm humanoid-upper-body robot, built with improved flexibility based on feedback from users of the earlier NEXTAGE OPEN series. It is adopted by universities and research institutions in Japan and abroad as an open middleware robotics research platform, distinct from the industrial-line NEXTAGE Fillie.

ARMAR-7 is a humanoid assistive research robot developed by Prof. Tamim Asfour's High Performance Humanoid Technologies (H2T) group at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT), continuing the ARMAR family begun in 1998. Running KIT's self-developed ArmarX cognitive software architecture, it understands natural language and gestures, autonomously unloads dishwashers, sorts laundry and performs other household tasks, and was demonstrated at Hannover Messe 2026 and the European Parliament's euROBIN showcase.

R1 is a low-cost wheeled service humanoid robot developed by the Italian Institute of Technology, sharing the iCub software API and aimed at demonstrating an affordable, safe-for-interaction research platform. It stands 1.3 m tall with an extendable torso (1.15-1.45 m), two 8-DOF arms with a 1.5 kg payload, torque-controlled force-torque sensors, and a sensor-equipped head for human-robot interaction.

Neoclone is Clone Robotics' next-generation musculoskeletal android, shown on the company's own site as the successor to its current Clone Alpha model and described as 'Clone's vision of a limitless future for human beings.' It is labelled 'in development' with no commercial release date disclosed. Clone Robotics, founded in Poland, is known for androids actuated by synthetic hydraulic 'myofiber' muscles rather than conventional motors.

Kuba is a bipedal research robot from Sber's Robotics Center focused on walking algorithms and dynamic balance, presented at the AI Journey 2024 conference alongside the Topa, Krab and Slon robots. At the time of its unveiling it had completed an initial 100-metre walking test as the team continued developing its locomotion.

Nurabot is an AI-powered nursing-assistant robot co-developed by Foxconn (Hon Hai Technology Group) with NVIDIA and Taiwan hospital partners, first unveiled at NVIDIA GTC in March 2025 and shown publicly at Computex Taiwan in May 2025. It is a wheeled, screen-faced humanoid with dual arms and a supply cart base built to fetch medication and specimens and deliver supplies, aiming to reduce nurses manual workload; hospital trials began in 2025.

HRP-5P is a full-size humanoid robot prototype developed by Japan's National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST) to perform heavy labor on construction sites, such as installing drywall panels. It stands 182 cm tall, weighs 101 kg, and has 8-degree-of-freedom arms that let it hold an object with one hand while operating a tool with the other, guided by a 3D-imaging head sensor that maps terrain and recognizes about 10 object types. AIST unveiled HRP-5P in October 2018 and displayed it at World Robot Summit 2018 as a research platform aimed at automating construction and heavy-industry tasks amid Japan's labor shortage.

N is the full humanoid robot platform from Highlanders, a University of Tokyo-founded startup building its own line of robot bodies (the bipedal Ninja series and HLQ quadrupeds) to feed its Kepler physical-AI foundation model with real-world field data. In July 2026, Mitsubishi Motors signed a basic agreement with Highlanders to jointly mass-produce a domestically made humanoid robot, targeting vertically integrated production of about 1,000 units per month at a Mitsubishi Motors plant in Japan during the second half of 2027.

Ai-Da is a humanoid robot artist invented by gallerist Aidan Meller and built in hardware by Cornwall-based Engineered Arts, completed in 2019 and named after Ada Lovelace. Using cameras in its eyes, a bionic drawing/painting arm and AI algorithms developed with the University of Oxford, it produces drawings, paintings, sculptures and poetry, and has exhibited at venues including the Design Museum London and the House of Lords.

Sara is a humanoid robot presented by Riyadh-based QSS AI & Robots as one of Saudi Arabia's first homegrown humanoids, first covered by Saudi/English media as early as February-July 2023 and widely reported in March 2024. Designed as a 162cm-tall bilingual (Arabic and English) female-presenting robot dressed in traditional Saudi clothing, she expresses facial emotions and converses using a proprietary in-house large language model rather than third-party AI; QSS CEO Elie Metri has said she is programmed to avoid discussing sex or politics.

Mohammad is a male-presenting humanoid robot made by Saudi company QSS AI & Robots, described by the company as the evolution of its earlier Sara robot and previewed at the DeepFest technology event in Riyadh in 2024. It is multilingual, introducing itself on stage as a 'national project' built in Saudi Arabia, and can take spoken orders and respond to queries; its public preview drew wide media coverage after the robot made unintended physical contact with a reporter.

Tomyris is described by its maker, Turkish company Biorobotec (working with Bursa Uludag University's engineering faculty via Ulutek Teknopark), as Turkey's first adult-sized humanoid robot. Standing 1.80 m tall, it was built in 40 days as an AI assistant prototype able to show nine facial expressions for more natural interaction with people; at its 2024 unveiling only its upper body had been completed, with full-body silicone skin and additional skills planned before an intended rollout as an institutional assistant robot.

DROF-o1 is a humanoid robot built by Vietnamese robotics company 1Robot, designed to learn factory tasks by watching a person perform them rather than being explicitly programmed. It runs on the company's shared Physical AI OS fleet-management platform and has been trialed on a DENSO assembly line, where it reportedly took over work from 15 fixed-arm stations after a few weeks of by-example training.

AI Worker FFW-SG2 is ROBOTIS' enterprise-class Physical AI mobile-manipulation platform, a semi-humanoid robot with a wheeled mobile base, dual 7-DOF arms, a 2-DOF head and 25 total degrees of freedom. It learns tasks from human demonstrations via imitation and reinforcement learning, carrying a nominal 6 kg dual-arm payload (10 kg peak) for assembly, inspection and logistics automation.
The H5S is Hiwonder's 16-DOF intelligent humanoid dancing robot aimed at entertainment display and STEM education, controllable via an optional PS2 wireless handle.

Berkeley Humanoid is a mid-scale bipedal humanoid research platform built in-house at UC Berkeley for learning-based reinforcement-learning control, distinct from the later, cheaper Berkeley Humanoid Lite. It demonstrates omnidirectional locomotion, hundreds of meters of outdoor trail walking, single- and double-leg hopping, and high reliability against falls.

Helios is a wheeled dual-arm embodied-intelligence robot from ROKAE, combining multimodal perception, SLAM-based autonomous navigation and whole-body force control for industrial, commercial-service and research tasks. The documented Helios II-5 configuration stands 1493-2000 mm tall, weighs 185 kg, carries two 7-DoF arms (5 kg payload each) on a 4-wheel omnidirectional chassis reaching 1.5 m/s, and runs about 4 hours per charge on dual 18Ah batteries, with an NVIDIA AGX Orin or Thor T5000 onboard computer.

Dyno is a humanoid robot built by VinDynamics, the robotics division Vietnamese conglomerate Vingroup founded in September 2025. It is aimed at security patrol, hospitality/guide duties and household assistance, with multilingual interaction, and was piloted at the Vinpearl Safari Phu Quoc park before its public debut.

The ASD-S2 is a 1.4 m tall, 31-degree-of-freedom humanoid robot from Chinese kitchen-appliance maker Aishida's robotics arm, aimed at research institutes and algorithm companies for embodied-AI development and validation. It carries a 5 kg single-arm payload, reaches speeds up to 4.5 m/s, and also supports human-robot interaction and entertainment demos such as singing and dancing.

FF Faber is an industrial-grade embodied-AI operator platform from FF EAI Robotics (Faraday Future's robotics division), built as a height-adjustable wheeled-arm manipulator with dual 7-axis arms and 26-35 total degrees of freedom. Its top Gen-4 configuration uses 6-DOF dexterous hands with up to 15 kg payload per arm, stands 1,300-1,600 mm tall, moves at up to 2 m/s and runs on an open Ubuntu/ROS platform with interchangeable end-effectors for manufacturing and material-handling tasks; it launched at Faraday Future's 919 robotics event in 2026.

AIR01 ('AIR') is a wheeled humanoid robot with a torso and two soft, tendon-driven arms from Swiss EPFL spin-out Embodied AI, unveiled at Humanoid Europe 2026 in Munich on 6 November 2026 for work alongside factory staff without a safety cage. Each arm weighs about 2 kg and lifts up to 5 kg; the robot starts under remote teleoperation on a customer line and is designed to take over tasks autonomously within about a month, reaching a 95% task success rate in paid pilots with electronics and automotive manufacturers; CE marking is planned for 2027.

HD Hyundai Robotics' first in-house intelligent dual-arm robot ('지능형 양팔로봇'), unveiled at the FIX 2026 Future Innovation Technology Expo in Daegu on 21 October 2026. Each arm carries a 7 kg payload over a 630 mm reach and ends in a human-like five-fingered hand; the still-in-development platform is aimed first at component bundling and assembly, with welding and painting planned next, running on HD Hyundai's own physical-AI model.

Taku is Dyna Robotics' semi-humanoid, dual-arm mobile-manipulator robot, publicly launched in September 2026 as the DYNA 2.1 Physical Agent built on the company's Dyna-2 vision-language-action model. It completes end-to-end commercial workflows such as warehouse pick-and-pack, hotel room turnover, food-service plating, and laundry folding from washer to shelf.

Quanta X1 Pro is a general-purpose wheeled dual-arm robot from Shenzhen-based X Square Robot, with 19 total degrees of freedom (6 per arm), a 649mm single-arm reach, up to 7kg peak payload per arm and an 8-hour battery life. It runs on the company's self-developed WALL-B embodied AI foundation model for household and logistics tasks such as folding laundry and parcel handling, and was named a CES 2027 Innovation Awards Honoree in November 2026.

handType: dual Sharpa Wave dexterous hands (22 DOF)
description: H2 Plus is Unitree's NVIDIA Isaac GR00T reference humanoid robot, pairing the company's H2 bipedal chassis with an NVIDIA Jetson Thor compute module and the Isaac GR00T software stack for academic and frontier humanoid research. It stands about 183 cm tall, weighs roughly 68 kg, carries 75 total degrees of freedom including dual Sharpa Wave dexterous hands, and runs about 3 hours per charge; Unitree announced it from Hangzhou in June 2026 for availability in late 2026.

Neo1 is a 4-meter-tall, 1.2-ton hydraulic-electric hybrid humanoid robot from Beijing-based NeodraDynamics (Qingzhuo Power), built by Tsinghua-background engineers using digital hydraulic actuators. It has 41 active degrees of freedom, a 500 kg dual-arm payload and +/-0.005mm repeat positioning accuracy, targeting nuclear, deep-sea, mining, disaster-rescue and heavy port/assembly work; it was unveiled at the 2026 World Robot Conference in Beijing and partnered with JD Industrial at CIIF 2026 for pilot deployment.

AGIBOT G1 is a dual-arm humanoid robot platform from Shanghai-based AGIBOT (Zhiyuan Robotics), distinct from the company's higher-end G1 MAX. It has an adjustable torso height of 130-180cm, weighs about 150kg, carries 20 degrees of freedom in the arms/body (26 total including head and waist), 6-DOF end-effectors that can be swapped for two-finger grippers, six-axis force sensors on both arms, an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 64GB compute module with three RGBD and five fisheye cameras, and runs over 4 hours per charge.

Magic WHR1 is a wheeled humanoid robot from Shenzhen-based Magic Cube Robotics (美丽魔方), designed for elderly and disability care and household assistance. The maker markets it alongside sibling embodied-intelligence care devices (Magic MHC1 rehab-assist robot, Magic TA3 bionic moxibustion robot and Magic US2 ultrasound robot) as part of a home-service and healthcare robot ecosystem; the product family was shown at CES 2026.

Orca is a full-size bipedal humanoid robot from Shanghai-based Cyan Robotics (青心意创), standing 1.45 m tall and weighing 40.5 kg with 28 degrees of freedom and a straight-knee walking gait. It runs the company's dual-arm collaboration model (reported 95%+ success on short tasks, 90%+ on longer ones) and what the maker calls the world's first "emotional gait" model, sharing the same Dino OS embodied-character platform used in its companion robot Amoo.

Qiyuan Q1 is a consumer companion humanoid robot brand launched by Shanghai-listed materials firm Swancor New Materials (上纬新材) through its Qiyuan (启元) robotics unit, alongside a quadruped sibling model T1. Positioned for home companionship, tech-hobbyist and developer use, Q1 began retail sale in China in September 2026 at a starting price of 19,999 CNY, with an "Explorer Edition" (Q1-探索版) variant for interactive play.

R01 SE is the base-spec version of Shenzhen Cyborg Robotics' full-size bipedal humanoid robot, built for hazardous-environment inspection, warehouse and industrial work. It stands 180 cm tall and weighs 75 kg, with 62 total degrees of freedom (6 per leg, 2 waist, 7 per arm, 16-DOF hands), an 835mm single-arm reach, over 400 N*m peak joint torque, a dual-arm payload above 20kg, fisheye/RGBD cameras, LiDAR and six-axis force sensing, a 12-core 275 TOPS onboard compute module, and a 48V 15,000mAh main battery with 1-minute hot-swap.

R01 PRO is the extended-runtime version of Shenzhen Cyborg Robotics' full-size bipedal humanoid robot, sharing the SE model's 62-DOF body and 20kg dual-arm payload but adding a larger 48V 30,000mAh main battery (plus a 3,500mAh hot-swap backup) for longer hazardous-environment inspection and industrial shifts. It stands 180 cm tall and weighs 80 kg, and can climb 15cm obstacles, 10-degree-plus slopes and stairs.

Primal M1 is a full-body bionic android from Beijing-based HokMind (泓柯智行), built by a team combining robotics, Beijing Film Academy and professional film practical-effects backgrounds to embody digital characters with highly lifelike facial micro-expressions and coordinated body movement. It is aimed at entertainment, brand and immersive-experience applications and made its first public appearance at the 2026 World Robot Conference in Beijing.

Primal F1 is a desktop-scale bionic interactive robot from Beijing-based HokMind, a smaller companion to the full-body Primal M1 aimed at personified, IP-customizable interaction for brand and entertainment scenarios. It made its first public appearance alongside Primal M1 at the 2026 World Robot Conference in Beijing.

A1 is an entry-priced bipedal humanoid robot from Shanghai-based Copilot Robotics (智可派), aimed at smart-education and home entertainment/companionship use with an open reinforcement-learning training framework and multimodal, generative voice/motion/emotion interaction. It stands 44.5 cm tall, weighs 8 kg, has 10 degrees of freedom, walks at up to 0.5 m/s, runs 2-3 hours per charge, and is built on an STM32 plus Odroid C4 / Jetson Nano compute stack with an Arm Cortex-A55 inference processor.

Robbyant R2 is the second-generation wheeled dual-arm humanoid robot hardware platform from Robbyant, the embodied-AI company under Ant Group, succeeding the company's R1. It has an omnidirectional-wheel chassis, weighs under 120 kg, reaches from the floor to 2 meters, lifts 6 kg per arm, carries six-axis force sensing and joint torque feedback at the end effectors, and runs about 4 hours per charge on swappable dual batteries; it is positioned as a hardware platform for Robbyant's LingBot embodied-AI model stack in everyday-service, logistics, retail and healthcare scenarios.

X7 is a working humanoid robot from Beijing-based DaxAI (大咖机器人), designed for repetitive pick, carry and sorting tasks in pharmacy and warehouse settings. It stands about 170 cm tall and can lift roughly 10 kg across its two arms; the maker also sells an X7 EDU variant for education and research use alongside its separate Qiji quadruped/wheel-leg robot line.

K15 is the second-generation general-purpose embodied-intelligence humanoid robot hardware platform from Beijing-based Wujie Power (无界动力, founded 2025), built around the company's own MWA latent-space world-model "universal brain." The maker says K15 is the first domestically developed embodied-AI robot to receive full industrial-grade EU CE certification across five directives, and it began bulk international deliveries in mid-2026 after the company booked about $100 million in global orders.

HMND 01 Alpha Wheeled is a wheeled industrial humanoid built by UK startup Humanoid (SKL Robotics Ltd) on an omnidirectional mobile base, distinct from the company's bipedal HMND 01 Alpha. The manufacturer states a 300 kg weight, 220 cm height, 29 degrees of freedom, 15 kg payload, 2 m/s max speed and 4-hour average run time, with a modular 12-DOF five-finger hand or single-DOF parallel gripper end effector.

Torobo-kun is a research humanoid robot from Tokyo Robotics with dual 6-axis arms carrying torque sensors on every axis, plus an optional interactive head module. It was an earlier platform in the Torobo line, predating the current full-body Torobo humanoid.

ugo Pro is a wheeled, dual-arm service robot from Mira Robotics with two 7-axis arms that can press buttons, operate elevators and perform card authentication across floors.
