It is built for security patrols, facility inspection and guide/reception duties in offices and commercial buildings, and its height can be adjusted via a lifting function.

ugo Nova is a wheeled, mecanum-drive humanoid robot from Mira Robotics with 22 degrees of freedom: a 2-axis head, two 7-axis arms each ending in a 2-finger hand, and a 4-axis waist. Aimed at factory automation, it handles kit assembly, inter-process transport and tasks like fitting and screw tightening, running on an NVIDIA Jetson Thor processor with roughly 6 hours of battery life from its LiFePO4 pack. It made its public debut in September 2026 at an AI Robot Association general-purpose robot event.

VS-MPR-01 is a general-purpose dual-arm robot from Vstone with a wheeled, four-wheel independently-steered base and a humanoid upper body. Its 28 motors drive two 7-axis QDD arms, a lifting torso, a 3-axis head and interchangeable grippers (each with an RGB camera), letting it reach objects from the floor to overhead shelves. It runs ROS 2 on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX computer, ships with a matching 3D simulation model for Sim2Real work in MuJoCo and NVIDIA Isaac Sim, and is intended for indoor use only. It was announced in July 2026.

HRP-4C, nicknamed Miim, is a bipedal android from Japan's AIST research institute styled on the average build of a young Japanese woman, with 30 body motors plus 8 dedicated to facial expression. It can walk, dance, sing and mimic facial expressions using speech recognition and voice synthesis, and was built both for entertainment demonstrations and as a human-proxy platform for evaluating products such as clothing. It was first publicly shown on 16 March 2009.

08-shiki Mobiloid (Type-08 Mobiloid) is a semi-humanoid research robot from HatsuMuv with a wheeled, independently-steered base and a humanoid upper body: two 7-DOF arms, a 3-DOF neck, 2-DOF torso and a lift axis for 30 axes in total. It is teleoperated through a wearable leader device from FuzzRoBo that mirrors an operator's arm and torso motion onto the robot, and is aimed at remote-manipulation research, motion-data collection and testing custom robotics control systems. It was first shown at the Physical AI Summit in September 2026.

OriHime-D is a 120 cm mobile avatar robot from Ory Laboratory with 14 motorized joints in its upper body, built so a remote operator -- often a bedridden or home-bound person using eye-tracking input -- can drive it forward and back, turn, and use its arms to grab and carry simple objects. It has been used to let people with severe mobility impairments work as remote staff, notably serving customers in Tokyo's Avatar Robot Cafe.

BINA48 is a head-and-shoulders humanoid bust built by Hanson Robotics in 2010 for the Terasem Movement Foundation, modeled on real person Bina Aspen Rothblatt. It uses 32 facial motors capable of 64 expressions, cameras with facial recognition and conversational AI to explore mind-uploading and human-robot identity research, and still makes public and media appearances.

Han is an expressive male humanoid robot built by Hanson Robotics in 2015, using the company's Frubber synthetic skin for natural facial expressions, facial recognition and multi-language dialogue. It serves as a research platform and public demonstration robot for Hanson's AI and materials technology.

Albert HUBO pairs a Hanson Robotics expressive head modeled on Albert Einstein with KAIST's HUBO bipedal walking robot body, making it one of the earliest full-body humanoid robots with realistic facial expressions. It was unveiled in 2005 as a joint research project between Hanson Robotics and KAIST.

The Philip K. Dick Android is a conversational humanoid robot built by Hanson Robotics in 2005 as a tribute to the science fiction author, using an AI trained on his writings and interviews to hold open-ended dialogue. It is a research platform noted as an early milestone in conversational android robotics.

Jules is an early expressive male character robot from Hanson Robotics, built in 2006 with Frubber synthetic skin to study natural-looking human facial expression in robotic form; it was used as a research platform for public engagement demonstrations.

Diego-San is an infant-like research humanoid built by Hanson Robotics with UC San Diego in 2012 to study cognitive development, motor learning and human-robot interaction by modeling how infants learn to perceive and move.

Robo Nano 2.0 is Milagrow's second-generation humanoid service robot for shopping malls, hospitality, airports, museums and classrooms, with flexible arms and head, a 13.3-inch display for animated expressions, and voice interaction for greeting, Q&A and wayfinding. It launched in India in December 2025 alongside two other Milagrow-distributed humanoids.

CHHAYA is a non-mobile humanoid robot torso from Asimov Robotics with an ultra-realistic animatronic face in silicone prosthetics, 20 degrees of freedom, multilingual NLP, phonetic lip-sync and synthesis of 15+ facial expressions, used for customer engagement, information and query-answering. A Chhaya-Lite variant offers just the animatronic face unit for integration into other humanoid platforms.

Humanoid dual-arm wheeled robot platform (AUBO calls it AHA3) from Chinese cobot maker AUBO Robotics, listed under the company's embodied-intelligence line for AI data collection, model training and factory applications. Each 7-DOF arm has a cross wrist, 3 kg rated payload, 648 mm working radius, up to 2 m/s TCP speed, EtherCAT communication and IP54 protection.

handType: 5-finger dexterous hands (15 DoF per hand, optional upgrade)
description: The TLIBOT T1 (also marketed as T1 Pro) is a full-size bipedal humanoid robot made by Sichuan TLIBOT Co., Ltd. (also branded FDROBOT), first presented in 2024. It stands about 1.60 m tall, weighs about 37 kg bare (about 43 kg with its 1250 Wh battery), and offers up to 71 degrees of freedom when fitted with its optional 15-DoF dexterous hands (41 DoF in the base configuration); the maker's technical spec sheet lists an 8 km/h maximum walking speed, an 8 kg single-arm payload when fully extended, and a leg structure rated to support a combined squat load of up to 145 kg (65 kg per leg). It combines 3D vision with LiDAR for obstacle avoidance, joint force feedback, and voice interaction, and is offered for OEM/secondary development as well as industrial, logistics and service applications.

Tianling L3 (天灵L3) is a humanoid robot made by Sichuan TLIBOT Co., Ltd. (also branded FDROBOT), standing 138 cm tall and weighing about 38 kg including its battery. TLIBOT debuted it at WAIC 2026 in Shanghai in July 2026 for university research and science education. It has up to 30 degrees of freedom with 7-DoF arms, a quick-release 612 Wh battery, an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 64G compute module running Ubuntu 22.04, LiDAR, and a 4-microphone array, and TLIBOT sells it in four hardware configurations (Basic, Qihang, Tuojie and Yuji editions).

Tianzhen Z1 (天真Z1) is a 167 cm tall, approximately 45 kg bipedal humanoid robot made by Sichuan TLIBOT Co., Ltd. (TLIBOT/FDROBOT), which debuted it at WAIC 2026 in Shanghai in July 2026 for commercial interaction and guided-tour use. It has up to 40 degrees of freedom excluding hands (5-DoF waist, 9-DoF arms), optional 6-DoF dexterous hands, mixed-LiDAR and depth/RGB vision, and supports NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin/Thor compute with MuJoCo and Isaac Sim simulation.

Y1 is a wheeled folding and lifting dual-arm robot made by TLIBOT (Sichuan TLIBOT Co., Ltd., also branded FDROBOT), combining a humanoid head/torso with two 5 kg-payload arms on a mobile wheeled base. It documents a 2470 mm work range, a 500 mm lifting stroke and LiDAR-based autonomous navigation with laser obstacle avoidance. It ships with a Jetson AGX Orin 64G compute module and ROS2/API secondary-development support.

Y2-B ("dual-arm pitch robot") is a wheeled humanoid-upper-body mobile manipulator from TLIBOT (Sichuan TLIBOT Co., Ltd. / FDROBOT), with a round wheeled base, a pitching torso column and two 5 kg-payload arms. Documented specs include a 2194 mm work range, a 700 mm lifting stroke and LiDAR autonomous navigation with laser obstacle avoidance, running on a Jetson Orin NX 16G controller with ROS2/API support.

Y2-P ("dual-arm elevation robot") is a wheeled humanoid-upper-body mobile manipulator from TLIBOT (Sichuan TLIBOT Co., Ltd. / FDROBOT) with a vertically-elevating torso column and two 5 kg-payload arms on a wheeled base. It documents a 2194 mm work range, a 700 mm lifting stroke, an 8-hour working duration and LiDAR autonomous navigation with laser obstacle avoidance, on a Jetson Orin NX 16G controller with ROS2/API support.

Y2-M ("dual-arm lifting robot") is a wheeled humanoid-upper-body mobile manipulator from TLIBOT (Sichuan TLIBOT Co., Ltd. / FDROBOT), sharing the Y2 platform's wheeled base and lifting torso column with two 5 kg-payload arms. It documents a 2194 mm work range, a 700 mm lifting stroke, an 8-hour working duration and LiDAR autonomous navigation with laser obstacle avoidance, on a Jetson Orin NX 16G controller with ROS2/API support.

Y4 is TLIBOT's (Sichuan TLIBOT Co., Ltd. / FDROBOT) fixed-stake dual-arm robot, a stationary half-body humanoid workstation on a ground-fixed or castered base with two 5 kg-payload arms (653 mm reach) at a 1100 mm working height, named by the maker for counting-type production tasks. It ships without an onboard battery or main controller by default, is powered from an external control cabinet, and requires a customer-supplied x86 PC (Intel i5-1340P chip, 16 GB+ RAM) connected via 2 Ethernet ports and 3 USB3.0 ports, with ROS2/API support for secondary development. TLIBOT markets this composite-robot line for gas-meter, electricity-meter and electronics-industry production lines.

T1 Ultra is a bipedal humanoid robot from TLIBOT (Sichuan TLIBOT Co., Ltd.), previewed as a new product at the 2025 World Robot Conference in Beijing in August 2025. Compared with the 71-DoF T1 it has a lighter 32-DoF body (3 neck, 7 per arm, 1 or optional 3 waist, 6 per leg), stands 167 cm tall, weighs 58 kg with its 2000 Wh quick-release battery, reaches 2 m/s and lifts up to 10 kg per arm; it carries 3D LiDAR, a depth camera, a microphone array and stereo speakers, with optional 6/10/15-DoF dexterous hands.

T2Pro is a bipedal humanoid robot from Sichuan TLIBOT Co., Ltd. (TLIBOT), listed on the company's Chinese product site with a sensor head, torso electronics module and five-fingered hands. TLIBOT has not yet published specifications or a price for it.

Xiaotian (超级物种-小天, "Super Species - Xiaotian") is a child-sized bipedal humanoid robot made by Sichuan TLIBOT Co., Ltd. (TLIBOT), announced on 2025-08-11 as the company's first model aimed at the consumer home market rather than industrial use. It stands 125 cm tall, weighs 25 kg, has 26 degrees of freedom, a maximum joint torque of 80 Nm and a single-arm payload of 3 kg, with onboard multimodal-AI edge compute plus vision and tactile sensors for obstacle avoidance. At announcement it was open for pre-order (99 CNY deposit) starting at 38,600 CNY, with deliveries planned by the end of 2025 based on order volume.

Tianxun X1 (天迅X1) is a bipedal humanoid robot from Sichuan TLIBOT Co., Ltd. (TLIBOT) with a racing-style long-leg design, which the company fielded at the 2nd World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing (22-26 August 2026) alongside its Tianzhen Z1, Tianling L3 and Y2 robots in autonomous racing and retail-service events. TLIBOT has not published specifications or a price for it.
